# Repository maintenance

Work only in `GoGoKo699/Partial-Monitoring-Capacity`. The owner authorizes
repository modifications and merging after checks. Preserve authorship, public
visibility, the MIT license and the exact Purpose/contact notice.

## Reading and scope

Read [AGENTS](../AGENTS.md), [README](../README.md),
[model and claims](../research/MODEL_AND_CLAIMS.md) and
[verification policy](../VERIFICATION.md), then inspect live main and open PRs.
Use a feature branch and reconcile newer changes without forcing a ref.

Preserve the receiver-only classical helper message, joint-register identity,
unconditional transmission error, average optical signal-energy convention and
predetermined product-measurement scope. Keep proofs, source attribution and
operational assumptions explicit. A scientific correction needs a linked record
preserving the earlier claim and explaining the change.

Reader-facing documents present the current scientific account. Put development
history and correction records in the [archive](../archive/README.md), and retain
revision-specific verification receipts in PR descriptions. Do not add progress
banners, task backlogs or narratives of research passes to the reading route.

## Verification and merge checklist

1. Preserve all [protected imports](../provenance/IMPORT_MANIFEST.json), reference
   reports, original assertions and tolerances. Review the exact diff.
2. Run the commands in [VERIFICATION](../VERIFICATION.md) using a fresh evidence
   directory. Inspect logs and every comparison difference; distinguish numerical
   agreement from byte equality. Inspect the rational certificate separately.
3. Inspect the actual published PR head, its workflow steps and downloaded evidence.
   Match the retained source ZIP and hashes to that revision. Merge only after
   successful validation, using the expected head SHA.
4. Verify the actual merged main separately. Record its exact commit, workflow run,
   artifact identity, source matches and comparison differences in the PR receipt.

Do not change repository settings, permissions, secrets or release state, contact
others, or modify another project without a separate instruction.
